linetext: ARBITRATOR:  Good morning everyone.  Can you hear me?  Thank
you.  It's 10.08 UAE time, on 3 June 2026.  I would like
to welcome you to the hearing, in this arbitration, AD
arbitration case 2025-002, between Flatiron General
Contracting Flatiron General Contracting and Al Saqer
Property Management LLC as respondent counterclaimed.
We will start by taking attendance.  I will start
with myself.  This is Claudine Helou, I'm the sole
arbitrator of this case.  We'll start with claimant.
You have already provided a list of your participants.
Can you please confirm who is participating, who is
showing already in the meeting and with the names.  We
will double-check with the list of participants that's
included in the hearing protocol.  On behalf of
claimant, would you please state your names?

have here in the meeting room with me, Mr Abdulaziz and
Mr Wajih, both of them attend here in the meeting room.

also.
ARBITRATOR:  Let me just check the name, Anes Bouchair?
MR BU SHAAR:  Yes, Anes Bouchair.
ARBITRATOR:  So this is on behalf of claimant.  On behalf of
respondent?

Mr Mohamed Fetyani as the legal counsels and from
respondent in-house, Mrs Hadeel Mohamed, and
Mr Syed Khaja, and from project Mr Tallal Alkhalil soon
they will be here.  That's all we have.  We have inside
the room, they are just coming now, Mrs Hadeel and
Mr Syed Khaja and Mr Tallal.
ARBITRATOR:  Okay, and they all joined already?
MR NAWAS:  No, actually, now we have Mr Tallal only.

timetable which is firstly we will hear the claimant's
opening statement, followed by a break, then by any
tribunal's questions, the claimant.
Then we will have a lunch break.  Afterwards we will
hear respondent's opening statement, followed by a last
break, and then any tribunal's questions to respondent,
followed by a procedural directions, if necessary.
Do you have any housekeeping issues you would like
to, you know, discuss or do you have any suggestions for
today's timetable?
MR NAWAS:  No, not from our side.
ARBITRATOR:  On behalf of claimant?
MR SAMIH:  It's okay.
ARBITRATOR:  So I think we are ready to proceed on that
basis.  Just please confirm from the court reporter.  So
the hearing begins with the claimant's opening
statement, Mr Samih, you have 60 minutes.
Opening statement by MR SAMIH
MR SAMIH:  Yes, we are about claim between Flatiron General
Contracting, which was engaged by Al Saqer Property
Management, to build a private villa, maglis and block
services.  This is in Bida Saif, farm number 2, in
western region in Abu Dhabi, and the contract was under
FIDIC 1999 Red Book contract.  The value of the project
was in the contract 12,483,733 dirhams, and the
completion period was with the 18 months.
The contract was performed and mobilised and built
by the time they employed terminated unlawfully in
August 2023.  Flatiron had completed over 71 per cent of
the works, confirmed by our independent expert report,
and yet also the employer refused to pay not only that,
the employer terminated the contract under false
pretences and assumed the rule of the new contractor
himself.  Used his own security and subcontractors to
inflate the cost and now seeks to recover this inflated
cost from the Flatiron.
One second.
The claimant ask for the tribunal to award
5.72 million, this is the total claim, excluding the VAT
5 per cent interest from 1 August.  The physical
completion, 71.1 per cent including all the material on
the site and the variations at the termination time, as
per the expert report.  And the extension of time, it
should be 164 days, revised completion should be
12 October, 2023, and the gross delay is 239 days,
employer responsible delays event.
Now, for the dismissed counterclaim, procedurally
inadmissible and without merit.  Wrongful termination
personally and substantially invalid.  Full costs legal
expert arbitral and administrative.
For the structure of this submissions, number 1, the
contractor procedural background, parties contract
essentials and arbitration history including the
respondent's failure to answer on time.  Number 2, the
employer, seven systemic breaches from delay, signing
and payment, wrongful extension of time rejection and
conflict of interest.
Number 3, wrongful termination, procedural and
substantive invalidity under FIDIC 1999 Red Book.
Number 4, the expert evidence under quantum engineer
Kaddoura's findings, claim valuation, and the
5.719,820 million entitlement.  The counterclaim and
final relief: procedural inadmissibility, merits
defence, and the relief the claimant respectfully
requests.
For the parties, contract, the letter of award was
in 30 September 2021 for the contract which valued
12,483,753 including VAT and the commencement date was
2 November 2021.  Original completion was in 1 May,
2023.  Governing law for this under UAE federal law and
arbitration article 20.6, it's Arbitrate AD.  For the
procedural milestones, legal notice of dispute,
20 November 2024; and request for arbitration in
30 January 2025; respondent's answer deadline 4 March
2025; respondent filed defence and counterclaim only
8 December 2025, approximately nine months late, without
leave.
About the parties, the claimant is the Flatiron and
the respondent is Al Saqer and the Al Saqer was the
employer of the project.  The contract essential key
dates, 30 September, the letter of award to Flatiron,
2 November, project commencement date.  But without
signing contract, only commencement date and the
contract still hold with the Al Saqer without signature.
1 May 2023 the original project completion date and
20 November 2024 the claimant issued legal notice of
dispute.  Claimant filed request of arbitration with
Arbitrate AD.  8 December, respondent filed defence and
counterclaim approximately nine months and the
respondent's untimely defence.
The tribunal direction for the arbitration timeline
very clear, yet the respondents failed to comply with
the stipulated deadline for their statement of defence
and counterclaim.
For the seven systemic breaches by the employer.
For the first one, late contract signing, 91 days delay;
impeded bond, guarantee, and mobilisation.  One second.
Date 30 September 2021, the employer only executed
the contract on 30 December, 2021.  Critical delays of
91 days.  The tender contractor signed the contract, but
the employer he didn't sign the contract and the
contractor at that time, he wasn't able to issue the
insurance for the project to start the project or hire
the subcontractor and sign the -- register the contract
in the ministry of human resource to assign
subcontractors, so all this time the project was hold
until the signature from the other side.
The administrative delay had immediate and
determined impact of the claimant ability commence work.
Impeded the timely provision performance bonds and
advance payment guarantees.  Significantly hampered site
mobilisation efforts, including procurement of materials
and deployment of works -- workforce.  Caused an
inherent delay of the project start date, setting a
negative precedent of the entire construction schedule.
For breach number 2, the advance payment delay, the
cash flow disruption.  79 days delay, the advance
payment crucial for early mobilisation and procurement
was paid 79 days late by the employer.  Caused severe
cash flow constraint on the claimant.  It delayed also
the subcontractor onboarding and site mobilisation;
directly contributed to the project delays from the
outset.
Breach number 3, interim payment delays.  The
employer's consistent delays in the processing interim
payment certificates created significant financial
strain and operational disruption for Flatiron General
Contracting, severely impacting project momentum.
Cumulative 106 day delay.  From the interim payment
certificate number 2 until payment number 12.
Subcontractor disruption: the persistent payment delays
lead to the cash-flow shortages, causing the critical
subcontractors to slow down or even halt work, impacting
their ability to procure materials and maintain
manpower.
Also, impact on critical path.  These disruptions
directly affect critical-path activities, leading to
further project delays and necessitating significant
efforts from the Flatiron General Contracting to
mitigate the cascading effects.
Breach -- sorry.  And breach number 3, design
modifications.  The employer, he already applied
modifications, structural and architectural for the
project in the municipality, from the submission date
until the approval date, 34 days' delay, which affect on
the project and disruption was compounded by lengthy
authority and resubmission and forced work stoppage,
causing significant cost overruns and hindering Flatiron
General Contracting's progress.
The changes directly impact key project milestones,
leading to an undeniable extension of time entitlement
of the claimant, which was later wrongfully rejected.
Breach number 5, wrongful extension of time
rejection.  Despite clear contractual provisions and
engineer's independent assessment, the employer
systematically denied legitimate extension of time
claims, impacting project timelines and the cost.
Contractual extension of time claims: Flatiron
General Contracting submitted valid extension of time
claims for delays directly attributed by the employer --
by the employer's actions and inactions, in accordance
with the clause 8.4 of the FIDIC 1999 Red Book.
Engineer's independent confirmation.  The appointed
engineer, after thorough review and validation of all
the submitted particulars, confirmed the merit of these
claims, recommending net extension of time 164 days.
Unjustified employer rejection.
Al Saqer Property Management arbitrarily and without
valid contractual grounds, reject the engineer's
certified extension of time, effectively ignoring the
building nature of the engineer's determinations under
FIDIC.
Impact on completion and the cost.  The wrongful
rejection imposed an artificial liability for the delay
on the claimant, disrupted the critical path, and led to
significant additional costs for the prolongation and
resource demobilisation and remobilisation.
Breach number 6, conflict of interest.  Undermining
impartiality through self-appointment.  The employer
engaged in a clear conflict of interest by unilateraly
assuming responsibilities that typically fall under the
impartial purview of the engineer.  This
self-appointment directly contravened the spirit of fair
contractual administration, removing essential checks
and balances designed to protect all parties.
This action created an environment where the
employer's own interests could, and did, override
objective project management decisions, impacting the
claimant's ability to execute works efficiently and
fairly.
Nomination of affiliated entities in bad faith.  The
employer nominated and engaged Royal Joinery for key
works without a competitive tender process.  Similarly,
SAMA was appointed for specialised services, also
circumventing standard procurement protocols.
These nominations were made in bad faith, directing
work to entities with direct ties to the employer,
ensuring non-arm's length transactions, and denying the
project the benefit of fair market competition,
transparency, and independent oversight.
Breach number 7, failure to settle the accounts.
Despite clear contractual obligations and the claimant's
written demands, the respondent consistently failed to
pay for executed works, certified variations, and
retained amounts.
This persistent non-payment significantly
exacerbated the claimant's financial strain, directly
contributed to project delays, and ultimately undermined
the viability of the project for Flatiron General
Contracting, leading to its eventual termination.
Termination was procedurally and substantively
invalid.  Procedural defects: No valid notice to correct
under sub-clause 15.1.  No proper cure period afforded.
No engineer determination under sub-clause 3.5.
Termination while project remained within an adjusted
completion period.
Substantive defects:  Engineer had confirmed
completion around 30 October 2023.  The project had not
been abandoned.  Termination notice: 19 July 2023;
effective: 1 August 2023.  The contemporaneous record
confirms no valid contractual basis.  The claimant
respectively submits that the termination was wrongful
in both form and the substance.
Procedural defects in termination - failure to
follow FIDIC 1999.  No valid notice to correct.  Denial
of cure period.  Absence of engineer determination.  The
termination was effected while the project was still
within an adjusted completion period, which the engineer
had formally confirmed.
Project status at the time of the wrongful
termination.  Despite the employer's claims, the project
was progressing towards completion, and engineer had
confirmed the adjusted completion date.  The termination
was issued prematurely and without valid cause,
contradicting an actual state of the work site.
19 July 2023, termination notice by the employer, and
alleging breaches by claimant.
1 August, the termination becomes effective.  The
contract was terminated by the employer, leading to
immediate cessation of the claimant work on the site.
30 October, the engineer confirmed completion.  The
engineer determined and confirmed the adjusted
completion date for the project, and indicating it was
within feasible timeframe.
No abandonment.  At no point did the claimant
abandon the site or cease works; progress was
consistent, albeit impacted by the employer causes.
For the expert evidence, expert Eng Jamal Kaddoura,
registered engineer, he is registered as an expert in
Ministry of Justice and he is arbitrator also in
Abu Dhabi Arbitration Centre.
Actual physical completion termination: 71 per cent,
not 55.63.  Gross critical delay: 239 days; net
extension after concurrency: 164 days.  Revised time for
completion: 12 October 2023.  Termination was wrongful;
employer demonstrated conflict of interest.  Contractor
is the net creditor.
For the expert analysis, expert methodology -- delay
analysis and physical completion.  Forensic delay  --
applied time impact analysis to reconstruct the project
schedule, identify critical path delays, and attribute
responsibility on the contractual provision and
contemporaneous records.
Concurrency evaluation.  Assessed concurrent delay
events, utilising Windows Analysis to differentiate
between employer-caused and contractor-caused delays,
establishing the net extension of time.
Physical completion audit.  Conducted on-site
inspections and detailed review of as-built drawings,
payment applications, and material delivery records to
accurately determine actual physical progress at
termination.
Quantitative assessment.  Calculated the precise
percentage of physical completion at termination by
verifying the executed works against the bill of
quantities, BoQ, and contractual milestones.
Critical delay analysis and revised completion.
Engineer Kaddoura's analysis meticulously traces the
cumulative impact of employer-responsible delay events,
demonstrating a revised time for completion
significantly past the original contract date.
Late contract signing: 91 days.  Interim payment
delays: 106 days.  Revised completion date: 164 days.
For revised completion date, net extension of time,
164 days establishes new project completion on
12 October 2023.  For the advance payment hold: 79 days
in advance payment led to severe cash flow constraints
and procurement slowdowns.  For design modifications:
34 days lost due to design changes requiring
resubmission to authorities and temporary work stoppage.
These events collectively resulted in a gross delay
of approximately 239 days, with a net entitlement to a
164-day extension of time, adjusting the contract
completion date to 12 October, 2023.
Claimant valuation -- total 5,719,882.99.   Head of
claim.  For the unpaid executed works plus retention,
3,002,531.20 dirham.  Confirmed variations and PS items
722,124.48 dirhams.  Advance paid to Blue Line
(subcontractor) 181,690.  Prolongation and delay costs,
1 million dirhams for the 164 days.  Loss of profit for
the remaining work, 15 per cent of unexecuted scope,
which is equal 541,309.  Subtotal, excluding VAT,
5,447,665.34.  VAT, 272,227.65.  The total due to the
claimant 5,719,882 dirhams.  Plus 5 per cent interest
per annum from 1 August 2023 until the full payment, and
the legal, expert, arbitral, and administrative costs.
Quantum breakdown.  Unpaid executed works and
retention.  A detailed breakdown of the 3 million, this
is the breakdown of the 3,002,531 dirhams claimed for
executed work and wrongfully withheld retention,
highlighting specific interim payment certificates and
the total retention amount.  In the interim payment
certificate number 11, outstanding balance, 502,531.
This is partial payment received, balance unpaid.  So
the payment certificate approved this amount and the
balance not payment.
In the interim payment certificate number 12, fully
unpaid, 1.5 million, certified works, no payment issued.
Retention fund withheld, 1 million, wrongfully withheld
post-termination.  The total unpaid executed work,
3,002,531 dirhams.
For the quantum details, the claim valuation
breakdown, key components.  A deeper look into the
significant components that form the claimant's total
quantum entitlement.  Confirmed variations and PS items,
722,124, representing all executed and approved changes
as well as provisional sum works, which remain unpaid by
the employer.  These were instructed works fully
completed by the claimant.
Prolongation and delay cost.  1 million dirhams
calculated for the 164 days of employer-responsible
delay (net extension of time), covering direct site
overheads, staff costs and equipment standing time
incurred due to project extension.
Loss of profit on unexecuted scope, 541,309 dirhams,
a 15 per cent loss of profit on the remaining 28.9 per
cent of the contract works (based on expert assessment)
that the claimant was prevented from completing due to
the wrongful termination.
These figures demonstrate the direct financial
impact of the employer's breaches and wrongful
termination on Flatiron General Contracting.
The counterclaim: inadmissible and without merit.
For the procedural objection, answer deadline was
4 March, 2025.  Defence and counterclaim filed on
8 December, 2025, approximately nine months late.  No
leave sought or granted; filing fee paid only in
December 2025.  The claimant submits:  The counterclaim
is time-barred and inadmissible.
Merits defence.  Liquidated damages, 573,000, no
uncompensated delay after extension of time -- LDs claim
is nil.  Completion costs, 7.7 million,
non-arm's-length; affiliated entities; upgraded scope
included.  For the project management company costs:
flow from employer's own conducted and wrongful
termination - not recoverable.
Counterclaim analysis.  Liquidated damages claim:
wholly unfounded.  The respondent's claim for liquidated
damages, 573,000 is entirely without merit as contract
was wrongfully terminated prior to the revised
completion date.
Liquidated damages apply post-completion.
Liquidated damages are only enforceable for delays
occurring after the contractually agreed-upon time for
completion, as adjusted by any valid extension of time.
Revised completion date, October 2023.  The expert
report confirms a net extension of time of 164 days,
moving the time of completion to 12 October, 2023.
Termination pre-dates completion.  The employer
issued the notice of termination on 19 July, 2023,
effective 1 August, 2023.  This occurred more than two
months before the revised completion date.
No grounds for LDs.  As the termination was wrongful
and occurred prior to the contractor exhausting its
entitled EOT, there are no grounds for the respondent to
claim liquidated damages.
For the counterclaim, counterclaim analysis --
completion costs and project management company costs
refuted.  Refuting completion cost: inflated and
non-arm's length.  The respondent's claim for
7.7 million in completion costs is unsupported and
highly questionable.  Non-arm's length: work was
performed by entities affiliated with the employer,
example Royal Joinery, and indicating a conflict of
interest.
Inflated scope.  The claimed costs include upgrades
and scope enhancements beyond the original contract
requirements, which are not the claimant's
responsibility.
Lac of transparency.  No evidence of competitive
tendering or justification for the rates applied,
leading to concerns about fair market value.
Refuting the project management costs: consequence
of employer's breaches.  The claimed project management
consultant costs are not recoverable from the claimant,
as they are direct consequence of the employer's
actions.  Direct result of the termination: these costs
were incurred only because the employer wrongfully
terminated the contract.  Employer's responsibility:  An
employer cannot claim damages or costs that arise from
their own breach of the contract.  No contractual basis:
there is no provision in the contract requiring the
claimant to bear the project management consultant costs
under these circumstances.
The claimant asserts that both completion costs and
project management consultant costs are and
unsubstantiated and directly attributable to the
employer's breaches, therefore non-recoverable.
Final relief requested.  The claimant respectfully
requests: Dismiss the counterclaim entirely, as
procedurally inadmissible and without merit. Declare the
termination wrongful.  Both procedurally and
substantively invalid under the contract.
Grant extension of time 164 days to 12 October,
2023, as confirmed by expert's delay analysis.  And
order payment of 5,719,882 plus 5 per cent interest from
the 1 August 2023.
And the summary of findings.  Systemic breaches.
The employer committed seven systemic breaches,
including delayed payments, design modifications, and
wrongful extension of time rejection, causing
significant disruption.
Wrongful termination.  The termination was
procedurally and substantively invalid, as the project
was not abandoned and remained within an adjusted
completion period.
Expert confirmation.  Engineer Kaddoura's report
confirms a revised completion date of 12 October 2023
and the contractor as the net creditor, reinforcing the
claims for prolongation costs.
Substantial damages.  The claimant is entitled to
5,719,882 for unpaid works, variations, prolongation,
and loss of profit, plus interest and full costs.
Inadmissible counterclaim.  The respondent's
counterclaim is time-barred and without merit, failing
on both procedural ground and substantive defence.
